title: Enterprise cost anomaly detection and action playbook
author: Maya Alvarez
content:
Overview

This playbook defines detection, triage, and remediation steps for enterprise billing and inference-cost anomalies observed against Redwood-hosted or Dedicated/Private deployments. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Support Engineers (L2/L3), and the Cost Ops oncall. Use this document when automated alerts or customer reports indicate unexpected token spend, embedding usage spikes, or model-switch-related cost regressions.

Goals
- Detect large-cost deviations early (target: detect >20% day-over-day spend delta within 60 minutes).
- Reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) for cost anomalies to < 4 hours for Class A incidents.
- Preserve customer trust with clear comms and remediation options (credits, rate-limits, rollbacks).

Scope
- Applies to Hosted API calls, Dedicated capacity customers, and Redwood Private control plane billing events.
- Does NOT cover non-inference billing (e.g., storage-only charges) — see Finance billing runbook.

When to use this playbook
- Alert conditions met from the Cost Anomaly detector (see "Detection sources" below).
- Customer reports a cost spike or unexpected raft of usage in support ticket or QBR review.
- Rollout of a new model/quantization profile resulting in large unit-cost changes.

Detection sources (inputs)
1) Cost Anomaly Detector (CAD) — primary signal
   - Triggers when a 1-hour spend exceeds 3x the 7-day moving average OR a 24h spend delta > 50% vs prior 7-day average.
   - Enrichment: customer_id, project_id, model_variant, region, pipeline_id, request_bucket (chat/generation/embeddings).
2) Token-level telemetry from Ingest Pipeline
   - High tokens-per-request rate or sudden increase in long-context tokens (>5k tokens) causes per-token unit cost blowups.
3) SDK / Integration Alerts
   - Client-side exponential retries or misconfigured batching can flood endpoints; detected via >200 TPS sustained for 5 minutes above normal.
4) Manual customer report or finance billing anomaly

Alert thresholds and classification
- Class A (Critical): Customer spend projection >$10k over expected next 24h OR sustained x10 spike in per-minute spend.
- Class B (Major): 200%–1000% hourly spike OR unexplained 3–10x token-rate increase.
- Class C (Minor): <200% hour spike or localized to a single non-critical project.

Immediate actions (first 60 minutes)
1) Acknowledge and owner assignment
   - CS owner creates/update ticket, tags #cost-ops, assigns L2 engineer.
   - Communicate ETA to customer: initial update in 30 minutes, hourly thereafter.
2) Triage checklist (parallel):
   - Verify CAD alert details and enrichment fields.
   - Pull billing projection run for affected customer_id (Finance dashboard: /dash/billing/customer/{customer_id}).
   - Query request telemetry for last 2 hours: model_variant, route, client_ip, sdk_version, request_size distribution.

Runbook: triage and remediation steps (detailed)
1) Validate scope and confirm impact
   - Execute sample query (SQL-like) in Telemetry Explorer:

      SELECT timestamp, model_variant, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate
      FROM inference_requests
      WHERE customer_id = 'CUST_12345'
      AND timestamp >= now() - interval '2 hours'
      ORDER BY timestamp DESC

   - Identify top 5 request signatures by cost_estimate.
2) Identify root cause vectors (check each):
   - Model change: recent rollout, canary -> check rollout timeline and revisions in Rollouts console.
   - Prompt explosion: repeated retries or user prompts that append context in loop.
   - Integration bug: SDK infinite loop or retry storm. Check client sdk_version and recent deploys.
   - Config mismatch: batch_size or max_tokens configured incorrectly for embedding pipelines.
   - Billing/config mismatch for Dedicated/Private: check reserved capacity vs burst mapping.
3) Immediate mitigations (choose minimal customer-impact step first):
   - Apply per-route temporary rate limit (example CLI):

      redwoodctl routes set-rate-limit --customer CUST_12345 --route "/v1/generate" --rps 10 --duration 2h

   - Enable auto-throttle on offending model (console toggle) to cap tokens per request at 2,048.
   - For Critical incidents, perform on-path fallback to a lower-cost variant (same quality tier):

      redwoodctl rollout promote --customer CUST_12345 --from modelX-v3 --to modelX-v2 --immediate

   - If a dedicated customer is misrouting to hosted endpoints, update routing policy and notify infra.
4) Cost protection and credits
   - For confirmed platform side issues, CS to propose a temporary credit (finance approval required for >$5k). Use credit template: /templates/credits/cost-protection.

Escalation matrix and ownership
- L2 Support: initial triage, run Telemetry Explorer queries, implement temporary rate-limits (Primary owner).
- CS Manager: customer comms and approval for service-level mitigations.
- Cost Ops (oncall): model-switch suggestions, immediate rollback authority for Hosted.
- SRE / Infra: network or Dedicated routing and capacity issues.
- Finance: approve credits >$5k or contractual adjustments.

Escalation steps by severity
- Class A: escalate to Cost Ops and SRE within 30 minutes. Daily executive summary to be prepared for customers with >$50k impact.
- Class B: escalate to Cost Ops within 2 hours. CS manager to own customer comms.
- Class C: L2 to resolve; document findings in ticket.

Communication templates
- Initial ack (30 min):
  "Thanks for flagging this — we've opened ticket #TKT-XXXXX and an engineer is investigating. We'll follow up within 60 minutes with initial findings and next steps."
- Follow-up (after triage): include root-cause summary, mitigations applied, expected impact, and next milestone.
- Post-incident summary: structured RCA, cost impact table, and recommended prevention actions for QBR.

Prevention controls and long-term fixes
- Alert tuning: reduce CAD false positives by refining model-variant baselines and segmenting quotas by route type.
- SDK safe-guards: ship SDK 2.1.0+ with client-side batching guardrails and exponential-backoff caps.
- Template rate-limits: recommend conservative default per-route rate-limits for new customers (10 rps per route per project).
- Automated rollback policies: enable canary auto-rollback when unit-cost increases >200% after rollout.

QBR and reporting guidance
- Metrics to include in QBR slides:
  - 7-day and 30-day cost trend, normalized by monthly active routes.
  - Number of cost anomalies, MTTR, and total cost delta recovered.
  - Top 3 root causes observed and prevention status.
- Recommended cadence: include a Cost Risk slide in monthly QBR for all customers with >$10k monthly spend.

Operational dashboards and canned queries (Appendix)
- Dashboard names/locations:
  - Cost Anomaly Center: /dash/ops/cost-anomalies (primary)
  - Customer Billing Snapshot: /dash/billing/customer/{customer_id}
  - Token Distribution Explorer: /dash/telemetry/token-dist

- Example time-series alert (PromQL-like pseudo):
  - cost_rate_by_customer[1h] > 3 * avg_over_time(cost_rate_by_customer[7d])

Post-incident actions (within 72 hours)
1) Root Cause Analysis (RCA) doc: owner = L2 engineer. Include timeline, query outputs, config diffs, and mitigation rationale.
2) Permanent remediation: schedule engineering ticket for SDK fix, rate-limit defaults, or rollout policy change.
3) Customer-facing summary and credit reconciliation (if applicable).
4) Update detection rules and dashboards to reduce recurrence.

Appendix: example SLAs and thresholds
| Metric | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Hourly spend vs 7-day MA | > 50% | > 300% | Cost Anomaly detector / Cost Ops |
| Sustained TPS (5m) vs baseline | > 2x | > 10x | Telemetry / SRE |
| Token size per request | > 2,048 tokens | > 10,000 tokens | Runtime / Serving team |

Appendix: quick-reference CLI snippets
- Temporarily limit route:
  redwoodctl routes set-rate-limit --customer CUST_12345 --route "/v1/embed" --rps 20 --duration 4h
- Promote rollback:
  redwoodctl rollout rollback --customer CUST_12345 --model modelY --to-revision modelY-v12
